Goal: Dynamic Form with Staged Replacement
We're implementing a flicker-free dynamic form system for the Cognition Chrome extension.

Here's what we're building and why:
The Problem
Current: When users change a dropdown (like provider selection), the entire form rebuilds with `innerHTML = ''`, causing visible flicker and losing user state
Bad UX: Form flashes, user loses focus, has to re-select previous choices
The Solution: Staged Replacement
Render new form hidden alongside the old one
Atomic swap: Show new, hide old instantly (zero flicker)
Clean up: Remove old DOM after swap
Preserve state: Form values and focus maintained through tree properties
Technical Architecture
Data Flow:

tree-to-dom.

js: Captures `formData` and `focusedElement` in events, handles `focus: true` in tree nodes
ui.

inference.

js: Uses captured form state to rebuild tree with preserved values

Looking deeper at the issue - I think I found the root cause.

The `disabled` property isn't in `specialProps`, so it's getting set as an HTML attribute instead of a DOM property:



In HTML, any `disabled` attribute disables the element regardless of its value.
You need to set the DOM property instead.

Fix: Add `disabled` to `specialProps` and handle it properly in `setFormProps`:
